**The fix is commit `070fa8bca3b59292118da26461b3d2cfd9a06796`, merged as pull request #743 "RESTWS-1037: Fix PRIVILEGE_DENIED sentinel leaks into serialized lists, causing HTTP 500".** The PR's description matches your symptom: `GET /visit/{uuid}` returned HTTP 500 (No serializer found for class java.lang.Object) when a child resource overrode `getRequiredGetPrivilege()` and the caller lacked that privilege.

Before the fix, a `PRIVILEGE_DENIED` sentinel could be placed as an element of a serialized list or map. The serializer then hit an `Object` it had no serializer for. The fix makes a denied element make the whole collection or map return `PRIVILEGE_DENIED`, so the enclosing property is dropped instead of leaking the sentinel. Top-level pageable results skip denied entries. I inferred this mechanism from the diff and PR body; I did not confirm the sentinel's declaration at that commit, because a ref-scoped grep returned nothing.

The fix is in the REST module's `omod-common`:

- `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/ConversionUtil.java:363-375`: the collection branch of `convertToRepresentation` now returns `PRIVILEGE_DENIED` if any element is denied.
- `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/ConversionUtil.java:397-420`: the collection and map branches of the other overload do the same for each element and map value.
- `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/resource/impl/BasePageableResult.java:52-62`: `toSimpleObject` skips results that come back as `PRIVILEGE_DENIED`.
- `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/resource/impl/DelegatingResourceDescription.java:245-257`: collection-valued properties return `PRIVILEGE_DENIED` if any element is denied.
- `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/ConversionUtilPrivilegeTest.java:1-230` is the new test file covering these cases. It is not part of the fix itself.

Line numbers come from the diff's new-side hunk headers, so the ranges are approximate to within a few lines.

Related PRs #744 (merge commit `0644380dbce500f3e4b4f64742e9247c59629d77`) and #745 (merge commit `ab57d35718277f6489ed290b21b83e7a5273528b`) are cherry-picks of the same change onto other branches. RESTWS-738 and RESTWS-996 are also linked to these PRs, but they are not the fix.
